rates.our_rates_assessment:
CLINICAL RANGE (verified): Clinically observed AF inducibility is NOT a single number; it spans roughly 5% to 85% and is critically dependent on (a) population: no-AF controls (Oral 5%, Kumar first-protocol ~3.5%) < patients without clinical AF (Marquardt 30.6%, Kumar sustained 29.5%) < paroxysmal AF baseline < persistent AF (Kawai 51%) < paroxysmal AF with aggressive isoproterenol (Oral 84%); (b) protocol aggressiveness (burst vs decremental vs isoproterenol; cycle length; number of inductions — Kumar 2012 shows burst-sustained 14.8% vs decremental-sustained 41.2% in the SAME patients, no plateau after 10 inductions); and (c) sustained-AF definition (>2 s / >30 s / >=1 min / >=5 min). This protocol-dependence is itself Kumar 2012's headline and is the single most important caveat for any external-rate anchor.

RONEY 32% — SITS SQUARELY IN RANGE, EXCELLENT MATCH. Darma 2020 reports 32.4% baseline (pre-ablation) inducibility in 170 real AF-ablation patients using a burst protocol (300/250/200 ms, sustained >30 s) that is a direct clinical analog to a burst-pacing labeller — essentially identical to the Roney 32%. Marquardt 30.6% and Kumar sustained 29.5% independently corroborate the low-30s band for moderate burst protocols. Verdict: Roney 32% is clinically plausible and well-anchored; this fidelity item passes for Roney.

UW/BOYLE 7% (6/82) — ANOMALOUSLY LOW FOR AN AF-PATIENT COHORT; the repo's flag is correct. The UW/Boyle meshes are LGE-MRI AF-ablation patients, so the apt comparators are the AF-patient BASELINE anchors, and every one I found is >=30% (Darma 32.4%, Kawai 51%, Oral 84%). A 7% rate does NOT match AF patients; it matches normal controls / no-AF populations under a single mild burst protocol (Oral controls 5%, Kumar first-protocol 3.5%). So 7% is not physically impossible (it overlaps the extreme low tail of the literature), but it is well below the clinical range for the population these meshes actually represent. The most likely explanations are labeller/substrate limitations already documented in the repo, not biology: the UW cohort lacks native fibres and UAC (DATASETS.md), so it runs on a rule-based-fibre + PCA-UAC surrogate (PREPRINT limitation), degrading the reentry substrate; and/or the in-silico inducer is under-aggressive relative to clinical practice (single burst site, no isoproterenol/autonomic analog, short simulation window with a simulator-scaled 'sustained >=600 ms' cutoff rather than a clinical 30 s / 1 min endpoint). The practical consequence is that UW is underpowered (only 6 positives), which weakens the labeller's discriminative test on that arm.

TWO HONEST CAVEATS ON THE ANCHOR ITSELF: (1) These are IN-SILICO monodomain Mitchell-Schaeffer verdicts, not clinical outcomes, and 'sustained >=600 ms' is simulator-scaled, not 30 s wall-clock — so the anchor tests whether the labeller's BASE RATE is clinically plausible, not numerical equivalence. Roney passes that plausibility test cleanly; UW fails it (too low for AF patients). (2) Because clinical inducibility ranges 5-85% depending entirely on protocol, a wide swath of labeller rates could be defended post hoc — the anchor is a sanity check, not strong validation.

BOTTOM LINE: Roney 32% is well within the clinically observed range and closely matches a directly comparable burst-pacing AF-patient study (Darma 32.4%); UW 7% is anomalously low for an AF cohort and is correctly flagged as a concern, most plausibly due to the UW mesh's missing fibres/UAC (PCA surrogate) and/or an under-aggressive inducer rather than a true biological rate. Critically, neither rate threatens the project's central claim, which is a predictive NULL whose spine (validity radius rho and the rho ~ N^-1 scaling law) is computed from the graph Laplacian and requires no simulator label at all — so even a judge who fully distrusts the UW labeller does not touch the core result.

rateChecks.claim: Kumar S, Kalman JM, Sutherland F, et al. "Atrial fibrillation inducibility in the absence of structural heart disease or clinical atrial fibrillation: critical dependence on induction protocol, inducibility definition, and number of inductions." Circ Arrhythm Electrophysiol. 2012;5(3):531-6. PMID 22528047; DOI 10.1161/CIRCEP.111.968859 — n=44 SVT patients without AF history or structural heart disease; cumulative AF inducibility after 10 inductions 49.5% (any AF >=1 min) and 29.5% (sustained >=5 min); decremental-pacing sustained AF 41.2% vs burst-pacing 14.8% (P=0.049).
rateChecks.note:
SOURCE IS REAL AND VERIFIED via PubMed (PMID 22528047) and the AHA Journals abstract (DOI 10.1161/CIRCEP.111.968859). Citation metadata correct: Circ Arrhythm Electrophysiol 2012;5(3):531-536; authors Kumar/Kalman/Sutherland/Spence/Finch/Sparks.

VERIFIED VERBATIM FROM ABSTRACT: n=44 SVT patients, no AF history/risk factors; 10 inductions/patient; AF >=1 min = inducible, >=5 min = sustained; "After 10 inductions, AF was inducible in 49.5%, and sustained in 29.5% of patients"; "Decremental pacing was associated with a higher incidence of sustained AF (41.2% versus 14.8%, P=0.049)". Project correctly attributes 14.8% to burst and 41.2% to decremental. Burst=200ms x10s, decremental=200ms to shortest 1:1 CL x10s, both confirmed. "Incidence increased with each induction... not reached a plateau after 10 inductions" supports the protocol/definition/number-dependence framing.

ONE MINOR CAVEAT (does not defeat the claim): the "First/mild single protocol ~3.5%" figure is NOT in the abstract. It is plausibly read off the paper's cumulative-incidence curve (single induction rate is far below the 29.5% ten-induction sustained rate), but I could not confirm 3.5% verbatim (ahajournals full text returned 403; PMC full text not opened). Recommend the project cite the specific figure/panel for that number or soften to "much lower after a single induction." All headline numbers the project relies on are fully sourced and accurate.

rateChecks.claim: Marquardt J, Marquardt K, Scheckenbach C, et al. "Prognostic value of atrial fibrillation inducibility in patients without history of clinical atrial fibrillation." J Atr Fibrillation. 2018;11(1):1837. PMID 30455834; PMCID PMC6207235; DOI 10.4022/jafib.1837. Reports: n=62 without prior clinical AF undergoing EP study, ~27-33 mo follow-up; 30.6% inducible (19/62); 18/19 sustained (>30s).
rateChecks.note:
VERIFIED — source is real and reports the exact figures cited. Confirmed via the PMC full text (PMC6207235, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6207235/) and PubMed (PMID 30455834). All bibliographic fields match: authors Marquardt J, Marquardt K, Scheckenbach C, Zhang W, Stimpfle F, Duckheim M, Maleck C, Seizer P, Gawaz M, Schreieck J, Gramlich M; Journal of Atrial Fibrillation 2018;11(1):1837; DOI 10.4022/jafib.1837; PMID/PMCID correct.

Every clinical number matches the paper verbatim: (1) n=62 — "62 patients matched our inclusion criteria"; patients had no history of clinical AF, undergoing EP study (retrospective 2011-2014 records), and it is explicitly a prognostic-value study. (2) 30.6% inducible (19/62) — "AF was inducible in 19 patients ('induction group') and not inducible in the remaining 43 ('control group')"; 19/62 = 30.6%. (3) Sustained defined as inducible episodes >30 s; "18/19 respectively 94.7% with sustained AF, 1/19 with non-sustained AF" — matches "18/19 of those were sustained (>30 s)." (4) Follow-up "~27-33 months" is a fair characterization: mean follow-up 32.5 months (induction group) and 26.7 months (control group), i.e. ~26.7-32.5 mo, rounding to ~27-33.

One minor caveat, not a defect in the cited claim: an intermediate search summary mentioned "AF >1 min in 49.5%" / ">5 min in 29.5%," which are different endpoints (duration thresholds across the whole cohort) than the 30.6% inducibility figure. The project's cited numbers use the correct 19/62 inducibility and 18/19 sustained figures from the primary text, so this does not undermine the citation. holds=true.

rateChecks.claim: Kawai S, Mukai Y, Inoue S, et al. J Arrhythm. 2019;35(2):223-229 (PMID 31007786; DOI 10.1002/joa3.12150) reports 51% inducibility (50/98) in persistent-AF ablation patients using atrial burst pacing with a >=5 min cutoff.
rateChecks.note:
CONFIRMED — real source, all details verified against PubMed (PMID 31007786) and the Wiley abstract (DOI 10.1002/joa3.12150). Bibliographic data matches exactly: Kawai S, Mukai Y, Inoue S, Yakabe D, Nagaoka K, Sakamoto K, Takase S, Chishaki A, Tsutsui H. "Predictive value of the induction test with atrial burst pacing with regard to long-term recurrence after ablation in persistent atrial fibrillation." J Arrhythm. 2019;35(2):223-229.

Clinical numbers verified verbatim: n=98 persistent-AF patients (61 yrs, 77 male) undergoing PVAI-based catheter ablation. Atrial burst pacing = 30-beat bursts from coronary sinus, 240 to 320 ppm. Inducibility defined as AF/AT lasting >=5 minutes after burst pacing. Result: "AF/AT was induced in 50 patients (51%)." This matches the cited "51% inducible (50/98) at >=5 min cutoff" precisely — 50/98 = 51.0%.

The study's own conclusion is that inducibility did NOT predict long-term recurrence overall (P=0.65), which does not affect the accuracy of the cited inducibility rate but is worth noting if the project frames this source as supporting inducibility as a predictor. The cited fact (the 51%/50-of-98 rate and protocol) is accurate as stated. holds=true.

rateChecks.claim: Oral H, Crawford T, Frederick M, et al. "Inducibility of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation by isoproterenol and its relation to the mode of onset of atrial fibrillation." J Cardiovasc Electrophysiol. 2008;19(5):466-470 (PMID 18266669; DOI 10.1111/j.1540-8167.2007.01089.x). Cited as: PAF n=80 vs controls without AF n=20, isoproterenol provocation; PAF 84% inducible (67/80); controls 5% (1/20); isoproterenol sensitivity 88%, specificity 95%.
rateChecks.note:
SOURCE IS REAL AND CORRECTLY ATTRIBUTED. Confirmed via PubMed (PMID 18266669) and Wiley: authors Oral H, Crawford T, Frederick M, et al.; J Cardiovasc Electrophysiol 2008;19(5):466-470; DOI 10.1111/j.1540-8167.2007.01089.x — all match exactly.

NUMBERS CONFIRMED VERBATIM FROM ABSTRACT:
- Cohort: 80 PAF patients and 20 control subjects with no history of AF, dosed with isoproterenol at 5/10/15/20 ug/min. MATCH.
- Sensitivity 88% and specificity 95%. MATCH (quoted verbatim: "high sensitivity (88%) and specificity (95%)").
- Controls: "AF was induced by isoproterenol in one patient (5%)" among the 20 controls. MATCH for "5% (1/20)".

ONE NUANCE ON THE "84% (67/80)" FIGURE (not an error, but worth flagging honestly): The paper's own headline induction/sensitivity number is 88%. Its dose-yield table reports the 20 ug/min yield as "88% (67/76)" — denominator 76, not 80, because patient counts shrank across the dose escalation (80 -> 80 -> 78 -> 76). The project's "84% (67/80)" is a legitimate DERIVED crude induction rate: 67 total induced out of the full 80-patient PAF cohort = 83.75% ~ 84%. This numerator/denominator is directly supported by the abstract's subtype breakdown, which sums exactly to 67/80 (vagotonic 15/17 + adrenergic 11/11 + random 41/52 = 67 of 80). So 67/80=84% and 67/76=88% are two honest framings of the SAME induced count (67); the project cites both correctly and separately (84% inducible AND 88% sensitivity). Nothing fabricated. If a judge asks, the defensible statement is: 67 of 80 PAF patients (84%) had AF induced overall; the paper's reported sensitivity was 88% (67/76 completing full dose escalation), specificity 95%, with 1/20 (5%) controls induced.

rateChecks.claim: Liu H, Yuan P, Zhu X, Fu L, Hong K, Hu J. Is atrial fibrillation noninducibility by burst pacing after catheter ablation associated with reduced clinical recurrence? A systematic review and meta-analysis. J Am Heart Assoc. 2020;9(14):e015260. PMID 32654581; DOI 10.1161/JAHA.119.015260 — reports ~42% inducible after ablation (1160/2772 across 12 prospective cohorts).
rateChecks.note:
SOURCE IS REAL AND VERIFIED. Confirmed via PubMed (pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32654581) and the AHA Journals page (ahajournals.org/doi/10.1161/JAHA.119.015260). Every bibliographic element matches exactly: title, all six authors (Hualong Liu, Ping Yuan, Xin Zhu, Linghua Fu, Kui Hong, Jinzhu Hu), journal (J Am Heart Assoc), year (2020), volume 9, issue 14, article e015260, PMID 32654581, DOI 10.1161/JAHA.119.015260.

THE NUMBERS CHECK OUT. The abstract states the meta-analysis included 12 prospective cohort studies, with AF noninducibility n=1612 and AF inducibility n=1160. Total pooled = 1612 + 1160 = 2772, matching the stated N. The "inducible" figure 1160/2772 = 41.8% ≈ 42%, so the "~42% inducible after ablation (1160/2772)" statement is arithmetically correct from the paper's own reported group sizes. The paper's headline result is the recurrence RR (0.68; 95% CI 0.60-0.77) for noninducible vs inducible patients.

FRAMING IS HONEST. This IS a post-ablation (not pre-ablation) inducibility population, and the project text says so. The paper did subgroup analysis by degree/grading of burst pacing (mild, moderate, severe), which supports the "documents protocol grading" claim.

ONE FAIR CAVEAT (does not invalidate the claim): The 42% is a DERIVED pooled proportion (total inducible / total N across arms), not a figure the paper reports as a single headline "inducibility rate." The 1160 and 1612 are the two comparison arms of a heterogeneous meta-analysis with varying pacing protocols and testing timing, so 42% is a rough pooled bracket rather than a protocol-standardized rate — which is exactly how the project frames it ("brackets the post-treatment rate"). No overclaim detected; number is legitimately traceable to the source. holds=true.

rateChecks.claim: Millenaar D, et al. "Inducibility of atrial fibrillation after catheter ablation predicts recurrences of atrial fibrillation: a meta-analysis." Pacing Clin Electrophysiol. 2021. DOI 10.1111/pace.14216 — cited as a real, findable source, with the specific pooled inducibility percentage NOT extracted/not verified (only citation metadata verified).
rateChecks.note: Source verified REAL and findable via PubMed (PMID 33686680) and Wiley. All metadata matches exactly: Millenaar D, Becker N, Pavlicek V, Wintrich J, Böhm M, Mahfoud F, Ukena C; Pacing Clin Electrophysiol. 2021;44(4):667-676; DOI 10.1111/pace.14216. The source genuinely reports that post-PVI AF inducibility predicts AF recurrence (pooled OR 2.08, 95% CI 1.25-3.46; 11 trials, 1544 patients; stronger in paroxysmal AF, OR 4.06). The project's honest caveat is accurate: no specific pooled inducibility PERCENTAGE is presented, and it is marked "not extracted/not verified." In fact the meta-analysis quantifies the effect only as an odds ratio, not as a pooled inducibility prevalence, so there is no pooled rate to extract — the project presents no fabricated number and does not overclaim. The hedged claim (real source, predictive association confirmed, specific rate not verified) holds.

spine.summary: The label-independent spine has a genuine label-free skeleton — on real atria the spectral gap λ₃−λ₂ is tiny (validity_radius_scan.txt: 0.0002–0.004), the single Fiedler vector φ₂ is genuinely ill-conditioned near degeneracy, and the gap shrinks with N — all computed from L alone, no simulator. BUT the load-bearing inference "rho≫1 ⇒ the linear biomarker provably cannot predict inducibility, so the core result survives even if you distrust the labeller" overreaches, and smuggles in assumption/label dependence at three joints. (1) rho's numerator ‖ΔL‖ is set by the Δw=0.36 knob — a CLINICAL calibration (perioperative CV-slowing, PRE_REGISTRATION §7.3, Heida 2021 PMID 34198544; the PMID/author/journal is real, the exact 20% figure is as-cited, not independently confirmed by me) — and rho scales linearly with it; meanwhile SFI enters the classifier as a per-region RANKING feature whose ordering is invariant to the global Δw magnitude, so the object rho indicts (a large-Δw magnitude estimate of Δλ₂) is not the object the pipeline scores. (2) rho only shows "single-vector φ₂ is ill-posed," yet the paper's own §9.3 says the well-posed fix is the subspace-SFI — and the subspace-SFI is ALSO null (ΔAUC +0.0028 at 100k); the actual null mechanism is feature redundancy with λ₂-alone/min-cut/percolation (PREPRINT §3.1), which is a LABEL-DEPENDENT empirical finding. (3) rho proves "SFI ≠ true Δλ₂," a linear-algebra fact, not "SFI ⊥ inducibility"; the bridge requires the premise that λ₂-fragility is the relevant axis for reentry — which the frozen prereg itself denies ("governed by wavelength, source–sink, unidirectional block — never by λ₂", PRE_REGISTRATION.md:121-122) and whose only physical warrant (Pecora–Carroll master stability function) is about oscillator SYNCHRONIZATION, the opposite regime from reentrant wavebreak. Honest scope of the spine: it proves "first-order SFI is a numerically invalid estimator of Δλ₂ on real atria," NOT "the biomarker cannot work." The biomarker null is real but is established WITH labels (redundancy), not by the label-free spine. Weakest points: the word "provably," and framing rho as a discriminating screening test when rho≫1 is nearly generic for any diffuse perturbation on any large diffusive mesh.

items.title: rho's numerator is the clinical Δw=0.36 knob, and it is irrelevant to how SFI is actually scored (a ranking feature) — 'computed from the graph Laplacian, needs no labels' is false for the numerator
items.finding: rho = ‖ΔL‖/(λ₃−λ₂). The denominator (λ₃−λ₂) is genuinely label-free from L. The numerator is NOT: ‖ΔL‖ is built from expected_dw = delta_w_mean_frac*(1+fibrosis_coupling*fib_edge)*w (sfi.py:239-240) with delta_w_mean_frac=0.36, a literature-CALIBRATED perioperative-stress assumption (PRE_REGISTRATION §7.3: f_CV≈0.20 -> f_D=0.36, citing Heida 2021 PMID 34198544 — a real J Clin Med AF-CV paper; the exact 20% figure is as-cited, not independently confirmed here). ‖ΔL‖ scales linearly with delta_w_mean_frac, so atrial rho≈2422 is literally 0.36 × (a graph number ≈6700). Halve Δw -> rho halves; send Δw->0 -> rho->0 AND the first-order derivative (φ_i−φ_j)² becomes EXACT. Meanwhile SFI is consumed by GBT/logistic as a per-region ranking covariate (sfi_region), whose ordering across regions is invariant to the global Δw magnitude (GBT is monotone-invariant; LR is scale-invariant post-standardization). So the validity radius indicts SFI-as-a-magnitude-estimate-of-Δλ₂-under-a-large-perioperative-field, but the pipeline uses SFI-as-a-Δw-magnitude-invariant-ranking-field. 'rho≫1 ⇒ biomarker provably cannot work' conflates 'biased magnitude estimator' with 'useless ranking feature' — a biased estimator can still rank fine. The spine is not purely graph-derived: its numerator carries a clinical knob that is orthogonal to how the feature is scored.
items.action: Recompute rho in the Δw->0 limit (pure derivative), where the feature is exact and rho vanishes, and show the region RANKING is essentially unchanged vs Δw=0.36 — proving the classifier consumes the exact-derivative object, not the finite-Δw one. Reframe the claim to its true scope: rho indicts SFI as a quantitative predictor of the λ₂ drop under a specific perioperative field, NOT SFI as a ranking covariate. Publish a rho-vs-Δw curve so the reader sees rho≈2422 is a chosen-magnitude artifact, and state explicitly that the primary ΔAUC ranking test does not depend on rho.

items.title: The well-posed subspace-SFI is immune to the rho argument yet is still null — so the label-free spine does NOT explain the null that actually matters; the real mechanism (feature redundancy) needs labels
items.finding: SFI_THEORY §9.3 concedes that for ρ≳1 the single vector φ₂ is ill-posed and '§5's basis-independent subspace SFI is the only well-defined object.' rho therefore only explains why the SINGLE-VECTOR estimate degrades. But the subspace-SFI — well-defined at ANY rho — is ALSO null (PREPRINT §3.1: FHN up to 100k, subspace ΔAUC +0.0028; power_analysis: needs ~4150 cases). So the label-free spine mechanistically explains the null of a variant the paper itself declares ill-posed, while leaving unexplained the null of the well-posed variant — the one a skeptical judge should care about. The paper's actual explanation for the subspace null is given elsewhere and is LABEL-DEPENDENT: PREPRINT §3.1, 'SFI ≡ connectivity information already available from standard graph features' (λ₂-alone, min-cut, percolation), a redundancy that can only be established by running classifiers against those competitors on the simulator labels. Hence 'the core result survives even if a judge distrusts the labeller' is false for the operative null: the mechanism that kills the well-posed feature (redundancy) is a labelled finding; rho covers only the ill-posed variant.
items.action: State plainly that rho explains single-vector ill-posedness only, and that the subspace-SFI null is explained by feature redundancy — a label-dependent result — not by rho. Stop presenting rho as 'the mechanistic reason the null happens' without qualifying it to the single-vector case. If a label-free account of the subspace null is wanted, derive it from graph redundancy directly: show subspace-SFI is a near-deterministic function of λ₂-alone/min-cut/percolation ON THESE GRAPHS (an R² computable without any labels), which would be a genuinely label-independent explanation and far stronger than rho.

items.title: rho proves 'SFI ≠ true Δλ₂' (linear algebra), not 'SFI ⊥ inducibility'; the relevance-to-reentry premise is smuggled — and the prereg's own label mechanism runs 'never by λ₂'
items.finding: The validity radius is a numerical-linear-algebra statement: first-order Δλ₂ is inaccurate when ρ≫1. Converting that into 'cannot predict inducibility' needs two premises external to the graph: (i) the quantity relevant to reentry is (an estimate of) λ₂-fragility, and (ii) SFI's job is to estimate it. Both are label-dependent. Damningly, the project's own FROZEN prereg contradicts (i): PRE_REGISTRATION.md:121-122 states reentry is 'governed by wavelength (CV×ERP), source–sink mismatch and unidirectional block — never by λ₂.' And the only physical warrant for the λ₂ axis (SFI_THEORY §0: Pecora–Carroll master stability function; Barahona–Pecora eigenratio) concerns SYNCHRONIZATION of coupled oscillators onto a common state — the opposite dynamical regime from reentrant wavebreak/rotors. So even a PERFECTLY VALID (ρ≪1) λ₂-fragility marker would have no guaranteed bearing on these labels; rho being huge or tiny is beside the point. The label-free spine proves a fact about first-order eigenvalue perturbation, and lets it stand in for the biomarker claim; the inducibility relevance is exactly what labels are needed to test — and did test, returning the null.
items.action: Split the two claims in the paper and never let one proxy for the other: (A) label-free — 'first-order SFI is an invalid estimator of Δλ₂ on real atria (ρ≫1)'; (B) label-dependent — 'λ₂-fragility carries no incremental inducibility signal.' Acknowledge that the MSF/synchronizability warrant addresses a DIFFERENT dynamical question than reentry, and that the frozen prereg's own label mechanism is λ₂-independent — so the a priori physical prior for SFI was weak regardless of ρ. Drop 'provably cannot work' in favor of 'is provably an invalid Δλ₂ estimator; its inducibility null is a separate, labelled result.'

items.title: rho≫1 is nearly generic (operator-norm over a size-driven tiny gap), so the 'screening test' has little discriminating content — 2422 is largely an N-and-norm artifact, not a discovered property of atria
items.finding: The denominator λ₃−λ₂ is a global low-frequency gap that shrinks ~1/N on any diffusive 2-manifold (rho_scaling.json atrial: gap 0.0209 at n=424 -> 0.00105 at n=7020). The numerator is the OPERATOR norm (max |eigenvalue|) of the perturbation Laplacian (gm4.py:241 eigsh k=1 LM; gm3.py:259 max|eigvalsh|), which is O(the largest local uncoupling), essentially N-independent. So rho ≈ (an O(1) local quantity)/(an O(1/N) global gap) ~ O(N), and exceeds 1 for essentially ANY nonzero diffuse perturbation on ANY sufficiently large mesh — including graphs where a Fiedler-derived ranking feature would be perfectly serviceable. rho≫1 thus fails to discriminate 'this marker will fail' from 'this marker is fine'; the proposed a-priori screening test fires on nearly every large diffusive mesh by construction. 'atrial ρ≈2422' is better read as 'n≈2000 with an operator-max numerator' than as pathology-specific.
items.action: Either demonstrate discrimination or retract the 'screening test any spectral biomarker can be subjected to' framing (SFI_THEORY §9.3). Concretely: exhibit at least one realistic medium/marker where ρ≫1 YET the linear marker retains incremental signal (or prove none can). Replace the raw operator-max numerator with the quantity that actually governs the second-order error — the Rayleigh coupling |φ₂ᵀΔLφ₃| (from §9.2), not ‖ΔL‖ — which does not over-state φ₃ coupling; report rho on that basis. If rho≫1 is always true on real tissue, say so explicitly: an always-true screen is not a diagnostic.

items.title: ρ*≈3 is calibrated on a 16-node path graph (with admittedly problem-dependent constant c), so the '10³× past validity' multiplier compares incommensurable objects; and the Δw field is fibrosis-weighted, sharing the label's dominant driver
items.finding: ρ*≈3 (the 10%-error crossing) is measured in validity_radius_sweep on a path graph P₁₆ with the first 3 edges reduced (gm3.py:228-276) — a simple-λ₂, localized-block toy. §9.3 states relative error ≈ (1/c)·ρ with c 'problem-dependent ... why ρ* is calibrated empirically.' A path graph's φ₂/ΔL alignment (c) has no necessary relation to a real atrium's diffuse fibrosis-weighted field, so ρ*≈3 does not transfer; yet 'atrial ρ≈2422 is ~10³× past ρ*≈3' multiplies a path-graph THRESHOLD against a real-mesh VALUE — different operators, geometries, and perturbation structures. Separately, Δw is fibrosis-weighted (sfi.py:239, fibrosis_coupling=1.0), and fibrosis is the label's dominant driver (PRE_REGISTRATION §7.4 Spearman(fibrosis, reentry)=0.75; e6 Morris: label most sensitive to d0 then fibrosis density). So rho's numerator is not independent of the field that generates the labels: the 'label-independent' spine shares the fibrosis substrate with the labeller, and a judge who distrusts the fibrosis model distrusts both simultaneously. Independence from the SIMULATOR is not independence from the shared fibrosis modeling.
items.action: Recompute ρ* directly on the actual atrial meshes (exact Δλ₂ vs first-order across a Δw sweep on real geometry) so the threshold and the value live on the same object; report the measured alignment constant c on real anatomy. Recompute rho with a UNIFORM (non-fibrosis-weighted) Δw to show the validity verdict does not hinge on the label-correlated weighting. State the precise scope: rho is independent of the simulator, but NOT of the fibrosis model that both rho and the labels consume.

items.title: The ρ scaling law is fit on the UNWEIGHTED combinatorial Laplacian, not the weighted conduction Laplacian rho uses; and 2 of 3 media miss their own Weyl prediction under fragile n=5 fits
items.finding: rho_scaling._laplacian_gap builds L = diag(deg) − A from an UNWEIGHTED adjacency of ones (rho_scaling.py:42-50), so 'atrial gap ∝ N^−1.05 matches Weyl 2-manifold −1.0' is a property of the COMBINATORIAL Laplacian — a different operator from the fibre-anisotropic, fibrosis-attenuated weighted conduction Laplacian L=D−W on which rho's gap is actually computed (validity_radius_scan gaps 0.0002–0.004). The Weyl-match is on the wrong operator relative to the biomarker. Moreover only the atrial curve matches: rho_scaling.json 2-D RGG fits N^−1.81 vs its Weyl −1.0 (81% off), 3-D RGG N^−0.84 vs −0.67 (25% off), and the d3 rows are NON-MONOTONE (gap rises 0.0203 at N=300 -> 0.0239 at N=600) under an n=5 log-log fit. The text (SFI_THEORY §10) spins the misses as 'collapse even faster ... at least as fast as Weyl' — directionally defensible, but it means the 'law' is one matched exponent (the headline atrial curve) flanked by two that miss their own predictions.
items.action: Recompute the scaling law on the WEIGHTED conduction Laplacian to match the operator rho uses; add more N points and report confidence intervals on the exponents. Present the RGG exponents honestly as 'faster-than-Weyl, not Weyl-matching' rather than adjacent to a 'matches Weyl −1.0' headline. The load-bearing corollary (gap shrinks with N, so rho grows with resolution) survives; scope the 'matches Weyl −1.0' claim to the single atrial curve computed on the correct operator.

complete.summary: Completeness/defensibility audit of AtrialSpectralBench for ISEF. The project's honest core is sound: the pre-registration is genuinely git-tagged before labels (prereg-frozen-20260720), the primary baseline in PRE_REGISTRATION.md §5 is the full 6-competitor set (so the preprint's "full competitors" primary test is faithful, not a goalpost move), every headline number traces to a results/*.json file (no fabrication found), and the cited references (incl. the less-canonical Bomela et al. Sci Rep 2020 seizure detector) are real. The label-independent validity-radius/rho spine survives any distrust of the labeller. BUT a hostile expert has real openings, ranked below. The two strongest are NOT fully addressed in the writeup: (1) the labeller's inducible fraction COLLAPSES toward zero as the mesh is refined (convergence_summary.json: 8.3%->4.2%->0% at 1500/3000/6000 nodes), the newer convergence run contradicts the older one (labeller_convergence.json shows 37.5% at 1500 nodes, ~4.5x higher), and the "verdict agreement climbing to 1.0" reassurance is actually a low-base-rate artifact (a constant "never inducible" predictor scores ~92-96% agreement when the positive rate is ~4-8%); and (2) the confident "predictive null / clinically undetectable, ~4150 patients" headline is carried by the SYNTHETIC FHN effect (+0.003), while the real-cohort GBT point estimates are +0.036 to +0.103, and the combined-cohort GBT ΔAUC = +0.051 actually EXCEEDS the pre-registered 0.05 effect-size bar (failing only on significance, p=0.16) — so the real atrial data is underpowered to exclude a meaningful effect, not a demonstrated absence of one. Fidelity item 2 (external inducibility-rate anchor) is genuinely absent from the writeup; I supply defensible numbers and sources. Severity: 1 critical, 2 high, 5 medium, 1 low.

items.title: Labeller inducibility collapses toward zero under mesh refinement; the two convergence artifacts contradict each other and the 'agreement' metric is a low-base-rate mirage
items.finding: This is the sharpest unaddressed attack and it targets the ground truth itself. Two convergence artifacts committed the same day (2026-07-23) tell incompatible stories. results/labeller_convergence.json (n=8, res 1500/2000/3000): inducibility 0.375/0.375/0.25, verdict-consistent 4/8 = 50%. results/convergence_summary.json (n=24, res 1500/3000/6000): inducibility 0.083/0.042/0.0, pairwise agreement 95.8% then 100%. At the SAME nominal 1500-node resolution the two runs disagree ~4.5x (37.5% vs 8.3%) and at 3000 nodes ~6x (25% vs 4.2%). Direction is consistent and damning: refining the mesh drives the inducible fraction DOWN, reaching 0/3 at 6000 nodes. The main-cohort operating point (~2000 nodes, Roney 32% inducible) sits at the coarse end where inducibility is maximal. The isthmus test corroborates (results/monodomain_isthmus_metrics.json: 0/27 inducible at 0.8mm; note explicitly says rotors die because 'the wavelength does not fit... numerical dissipation kills the rotor'). Worse, convergence_summary.json's interpretation ('verdict_agreement climbing toward 1.0 => the labeller converges') is backwards: when the positive rate collapses to ~4-8%, a trivial constant 'never inducible' predictor already scores ~92-96% agreement, so high agreement at the fine end is EXACTLY what a labeller converging to 'nothing is inducible' looks like — it is not evidence of stability. The preprint cites neither convergence result (§3.6 covers only E6 Morris/GP UQ). Impact: threatens the ABSOLUTE AUCs, the localization result (grad_phi2 KEEP needs real reentry origins), and the 32% external anchor — i.e. the positive class may be substantially coarse-mesh numerical reentry. It does NOT threaten the relative SFI-vs-competitors null (same labels both arms) or the label-independent rho spine.
items.action: Do not let a judge find this first. (a) Reconcile the two convergence files in the notebook and preprint: explain the 4.5x rate discrepancy at 1500 nodes (different subject sample? different solver settings? coarsening landing point?) and correct the 'labeller converges' interpretation to 'agreement rises trivially because the base rate collapses.' (b) Report the 6000-node 0% result openly as a limitation and state plainly that the absolute inducible fraction is a coarse-mesh-dependent quantity, so all ABSOLUTE numbers (competitor AUC ~0.83, 32% rate) are provisional pending the deferred fine-mesh/openCARP validation. (c) Lead the defense with the two claims that are resolution-invariant: the RELATIVE null (SFI adds nothing over competitors on identical labels at any fixed resolution) and the rho/validity-radius spine (computed from the Laplacian, no simulator). (d) If any compute is available, run the 1500->48000 ladder the git log shows was scaffolded (commit b20ee92) on >=10 subjects to establish whether verdicts stabilize at a NONZERO rate at fine resolution or keep drifting to zero.

items.title: The confident 'null / clinically undetectable (~4150 patients)' headline is carried by synthetic FHN networks; real-atrial GBT point estimates are 10-30x larger and the combined estimate exceeds the pre-registered effect-size bar
items.finding: The abstract's quantitative headline — 'ΔAUC ≈ +0.003', 'would require ~4,150 patients to detect at 80% power — clinically undetectable' — is computed on the SYNTHETIC FHN subspace effect (results/power_analysis.json: N=55000, subspace ΔAUC 0.00283, n_needed_80pct 4151.8). The real atrial data show much larger point estimates (results/gm1_expanded_metrics.json): Roney GBT competitors_vs_+SFI +0.036 (p=0.26), combined GBT +0.051 (p=0.16), combined GBT fibrosis_vs_+SFI +0.103 (p=0.009), Roney GBT fibrosis_vs_+SFI +0.069. Critically, the combined competitors_vs_+SFI grouped ΔAUC = 0.0507 EXCEEDS the pre-registered ΔAUC>=0.05 effect-size threshold (PRE_REGISTRATION.md §2) and fails the endpoint only on the DeLong p<0.05 half. The bootstrap CIs on real data straddle 0.05 (Roney GBT [-0.029,+0.096]; combined GBT [-0.014,+0.126]) — the real cohorts are underpowered to EXCLUDE a clinically meaningful effect, which is different from having demonstrated its absence. A hostile judge will say: your tight exclusion lives only in 100k FHN random-geometric graphs (which are not atria), your real-atrial GBT+SFI point estimates are +0.05 to +0.10, and the '4150 patients' figure is derived from the smallest number in the study. An effect of 0.05 (the real combined GBT) needs far fewer than 4150 cases, so the 'clinically undetectable' conclusion does not follow from the real data. The systematic LR-negative / GBT-positive split across every cohort also hints SFI carries nonlinear-interaction signal that the LR-led framing understates.
items.action: Separate the two regimes explicitly and stop letting the synthetic +0.003 stand as THE effect size. State: on real anatomy the primary endpoint is NOT MET but is INCONCLUSIVE/underpowered (point estimates +0.036 to +0.051, CIs include +0.05, p~0.16-0.26); the confident exclusion is a property of the 100k synthetic FHN cohort only. Run the power analysis on the REAL combined-cohort GBT effect (+0.051) and report the sample size that WOULD be needed if that point estimate were real — this is the honest number for 'how big a clinical study would settle it.' Explicitly flag the combined GBT +0.0507 as sitting on the effect-size threshold and explain why you still call the endpoint unmet (fails the paired-significance criterion at n=144).

items.title: The 'rho ~ 2422 so the linear biomarker provably cannot work' claim overreaches: rho bounds the numerical accuracy of the Delta-lambda2 VALUE, not the classification information in the feature
items.finding: The validity-radius argument is the project's proudest result and is mathematically correct as stated in SFI_THEORY.md §9 — but the ABSTRACT's phrasing ('real excitable media violate this by ~10^3, so the linear biomarker provably cannot work') conflates two different things. rho = ||ΔL||/(λ3-λ2) bounds the relative error of the first-order Δλ2 MAGNITUDE estimate (Davis-Kahan / 2nd-order Rayleigh-Schrödinger). A classifier does not need an accurate Δλ2 magnitude; it needs the feature to rank-correlate with the label, which a badly-scaled but monotone feature can still do. Two of the project's own results directly contradict 'provably cannot work': (i) SFI beats a fibrosis-only baseline at combined GBT p=0.009 (gm1_expanded_metrics.json) — i.e. the linear SFI demonstrably carries usable information despite rho~2422; (ii) the EXACT per-region Δλ2 SFI (valid at any ||ΔL||, no rho limitation, SFI_THEORY.md §6) ALSO adds nothing over competitors (gm3_metrics.json competitors_vs_+exact: all null). Point (ii) is the real, deep evidence that the null is about the science, not the approximation — and it makes the rho argument largely IRRELEVANT to the predictive null (the exact object fails too, for reasons rho does not explain). A sharp mathematician judge will pull exactly this thread: 'if rho proves it cannot work, why does it beat fibrosis at p=0.009, and why do you even need the exact-recompute experiment?'
items.action: Downgrade the causal language. rho explains why the SINGLE-VECTOR SFI is NOISY/ill-conditioned (φ2 rotates into φ3, Davis-Kahan), not why SFI is non-predictive. Make the logical chain explicit and correct: the predictive null is established by the EXACT-Δλ2 and subspace SFI ALSO adding nothing (computation-independent); rho is a separate, label-independent diagnostic of first-order invalidity. Change 'provably cannot work' to something like 'the first-order Δλ2 value is provably inaccurate on real tissue (rho~10^3 past rho*), which is why the single-vector SFI is noisy; the predictive null is separately confirmed by the exact object also failing.' Reconcile it head-on with the SFI-beats-fibrosis p=0.009 result so the judge sees you already thought of it.

items.title: Fidelity item 2 (external inducibility-rate anchor) is missing from the writeup — supply it, with the killer caveat that the same cohort's authors found acute in-silico inducibility does not track clinical outcome
items.finding: The preprint never anchors its inducibility rates (Roney 32%, UW/Boyle 7%) to any external number — it only notes UW is 'low.' A judge WILL ask 'is 32% even physiological?' The findable evidence: (a) clinical rapid/burst-pacing AF induction spans roughly 15-48% depending on protocol and endpoint — e.g. sustained-AF induction ~14.8% (burst) vs ~41.2% (decremental) reported in a burst-vs-decremental atrial-vulnerability comparison [sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1607551X12003038 — verify exact split before quoting]; ~20% inducible with a standardized protocol [pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2693942]; inducibility is protocol-sensitive and non-specific even in structurally normal atria [ahajournals.org/doi/10.1161/CIRCEP.111.968859]. (b) In-silico patient-specific models: Boyle-group Utah substrates were inducible from 2/10 and 3/10 PV pacing sites (20%/30%). (c) DECISIVE context: the very Roney virtual cohort used here — Roney et al., Circ Arrhythm Electrophysiol 2022;15(2):e010253 [pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8845531] — reported that acute simulation inducibility stress tests did NOT differentiate clinical AF outcomes. Bottom line: Roney 32% sits within the clinical/in-silico burst-pacing range and is defensible; UW/Boyle 7% is at/below the low end, confirming the team's own concern flag (and consistent with the resolution-collapse in finding 1). But even an in-range rate does not buy clinical relevance, because the cohort's own authors showed acute inducibility is a weak clinical proxy.
items.action: Add a short 'external-rate anchor' paragraph citing the sources above (with the CV-band citation Heida 2021 already in the notebook). State plainly: Roney 32% is within the reported burst-pacing inducibility range; UW 7% is below it and is flagged. Then pre-empt over-interpretation by citing Roney 2022 CIRCEP that acute in-silico inducibility does not differentiate clinical outcomes — this REINFORCES the project's honest framing (label is a simulator construct, not clinical POAF) and turns a vulnerability into a credibility asset. Verify the exact 14.8%/41.2% attribution before printing it; if you cannot pin the source, present it as 'roughly 15-40% depending on protocol' with the AHA/ScienceDirect URLs and mark the precise split unverified.

items.title: The UW/Boyle external cohort is uninformative, not a clean replication — 'two independent real cohorts' oversells a Roney-dominated combined result
items.finding: UW-only base AUCs are at or below chance (gm1_expanded_metrics.json: competitors LR 0.577 / GBT 0.382; fibrosis GBT base 0.116 — sub-chance noise from only 6 positives). When nothing predicts the label, an add-on test cannot show SFI adds or fails to add anything — UW-only is uninformative, not a null. So the meaningful external test is the combined n=144, which is dominated by Roney (20 of 26 positives). The abstract's framing ('two independent real left-atrial cohorts', 'replicated on real Roney and UW/Boyle cohorts') implies two informative replications when it is really one informative cohort (Roney) plus one underpowered/near-chance cohort (UW) folded into a Roney-weighted combined analysis. The one UW cell marked endpoint_met=true (fibrosis_vs_+SFI GBT, p=0.026, ΔAUC +0.34) is built on a base AUC of 0.116 — pure noise, and the writeup already says 'ignore that cell,' which underlines the point that UW carries no signal.
items.action: Reframe UW honestly as an external GENERALIZATION-of-labeller check that came back underpowered (7% inducible, near-chance predictability), not as an independent replication of the null. Report the combined n=144 as the external test and note its Roney weighting. Drop or soften 'two independent cohorts' language. This connects to finding 1: the low UW rate may itself be a symptom of the resolution/representation sensitivity of the labeller (UW uses a PCA-surrogate UAC and a different mesh source).

items.title: No multiple-comparisons control across ~30+ DeLong tests; the sole nominally-significant positive (SFI>fibrosis, p=0.009) is not family-wise safe
items.finding: Across gm1_expanded + gm3 the pipeline runs {LR,GBT} x {competitors, fibrosis} x {single, subspace, exact} x {Roney, UW, combined} = dozens of DeLong tests, with no Bonferroni/FDR mentioned. The project's one positive empirical claim that SFI is 'not merely re-encoded fibrosis' rests on combined fibrosis_vs_+SFI GBT p=0.009. Against ~12-30 comparisons, a family-wise threshold is ~0.05/12 ≈ 0.004 to 0.05/30 ≈ 0.0017, so p=0.009 does not clearly survive correction. Because this positive is used affirmatively (to upgrade the story from 'SFI=fibrosis' to 'SFI=redundant connectivity info'), its multiplicity exposure matters. The pre-registration commits to an effect-size gate but not to a multiplicity correction.
items.action: State the number of comparisons and apply an FDR or hierarchical (primary-then-secondary) correction, or explicitly declare the fibrosis_vs_+SFI test as a single pre-specified SECONDARY endpoint (PRE_REGISTRATION.md treats it as such) so p=0.009 is judged at the secondary level rather than the family level. Either way, name the exposure before a judge does, and note the sub-chance UW 'endpoint_met' cell is excluded as noise.

items.title: The rho scaling 'law' is five points per medium with a non-monotone 3-D series — it is oversold as a law
items.finding: results/rho_scaling.json fits gap-vs-N exponents from only 5 points each. The 3-D random-geometric series is non-monotone: gap RISES from N=300 (0.0203) to N=600 (0.0239) before falling, yet a single power law (-0.836) is fitted through it (vs Weyl 2/d = -0.667). The 2-D series fits -1.81 (vs Weyl -1.0) — far from the Weyl reference. Only the real atrial 2-manifold (-1.05) cleanly matches Weyl (-1.0). So the honest content is 'the atrial-surface gap collapses ~N^-1 consistent with the 2-manifold Weyl exponent, and abstract graphs collapse at least as fast' — which the notebook states correctly — but the preprint table framing ('a Weyl scaling law', 'the gap collapses by a Weyl scaling law') invites a judge to attack a 5-point, partly non-monotone fit as an overfit dressed as a law.
items.action: Add N per fit and R^2/CI on each exponent; show the 3-D non-monotonicity rather than hiding it inside a single slope. Restrict the strong 'Weyl match' claim to the atrial 2-manifold case (already the notebook's honest scope) and label the random-geometric exponents as empirical 'at least as fast as Weyl' bounds, not law confirmations. Add more N points to the atrial series if any cheap compute is available, since that is the load-bearing curve.

items.title: The localizer is oversold: the strict pre-registered localization endpoint is NULL for every field including grad_phi2, and grad_phi2's 'KEEP' is a weak, mechanistically-expected rank
items.finding: The pre-registered SECONDARY endpoint (median argmax geodesic error below the spatial-null 5th percentile, PRE_REGISTRATION.md §3) is NOT met by ANY field including grad_phi2 (gm2_metrics.json: grad_phi2 0.472 vs null 0.406). grad_phi2 survives only as a weak rank-correlation (origin in top ~18%: 100k rank 0.176; cardiac rank 0.168-0.284) — 'the origin is usually in the top fifth of the field,' not 'locates the origin.' It is NOT better than the raw substrate in 2 of 3 media (FHN fibrosis rank 0.099 vs grad_phi2 0.176; cardiac fibrosis 0.242 vs grad_phi2 0.168 — here it wins; Kuramoto grad_phi2 0.091 vs fibrosis 0.147 — wins). The team's own bottleneck experiment (notebook 2026-07-22, novelty ①) shows grad_phi2 and fibrosis coincide BY MECHANISM (the Fiedler bottleneck IS the low-conduction lesion), so the 'transfer across three media' is partly a restatement that reentry anchors at conduction heterogeneities — a near-tautology in diffusively-coupled media. The cardiac arm of the '3-media transfer' rests on only n=20 origins.
items.action: State the strict localization endpoint is null for all fields (already true, but make it prominent, not buried) and describe grad_phi2 as a weak-but-real, purely-connectivity-derived rank localizer that MATCHES substrate localization and beats graph-centrality baselines — explicitly NOT a precise localizer and NOT better than substrate imaging. Keep the honest bottleneck-mechanism explanation front and center; it is the strongest form of the claim. Fix the §3.4 table row labeled 'cardiac / FHN (100k, converged)': 100k is FHN-only; cardiac is n=20 — the merged label reads as if 100k cardiac networks were run.

Add a real, findable citation for the perioperative CV-slowing value behind Δw=0.36, or mark it 'calibrated, source unverified' — do not present it as an established literature constant without one.

synthesis.rate_anchor_writeup: Clinical AF inducibility is not a single number: across verified burst-/rapid-pacing studies it spans roughly 5% to 85%, driven by population, protocol aggressiveness, the sustained-AF definition, and the number of inductions. Kumar et al. (Circ Arrhythm Electrophysiol 2012; PMID 22528047) make this the headline — in the SAME patients, burst-pacing sustained AF was 14.8% vs decremental 41.2%, with no plateau after 10 inductions — so any external-rate anchor is a plausibility sanity check, not validation. Our Roney rate of 32% (20/62) sits squarely in the moderate-burst band: it closely matches Marquardt et al. (30.6%, 19/62 patients without clinical AF, burst pacing, sustained >30 s; J Atr Fibrillation 2018, PMID 30455834) and Kumar's 29.5% sustained-AF figure, and falls between the no-AF-control floor (Oral et al. 5%, 1/20; J Cardiovasc Electrophysiol 2008, PMID 18266669) and the AF-patient/aggressive-protocol ceiling (Kawai persistent-AF 51%, 50/98, ≥5 min cutoff; J Arrhythm 2019, PMID 31007786; Oral paroxysmal-AF + isoproterenol 84%), consistent with the ~42% pooled post-ablation rate (Liu et al. meta-analysis, 1160/2772; J Am Heart Assoc 2020, PMID 32654581). Roney 32% therefore passes the plausibility check. (Note: I deliberately do NOT cite the Darma 2020 32.4% pre-ablation figure here — although it is the closest analog, its independent verification came back unconfirmed, so I anchor only on sources whose citation checks held.) Our UW/Boyle rate of 7% (6/82) does NOT pass: it sits at the no-AF-control floor (Oral 5%), far below every verified AF-patient rate (Kawai 51%, Oral 84%), even though these meshes are AF-ablation anatomy — the repo's flag is correct. The most plausible causes are labeller/substrate limitations, not biology: the UW cohort's missing native fibres/UAC (PCA surrogate) and an under-aggressive single-burst inducer, compounded by the labeller's documented resolution sensitivity (inducible fraction 8.3%→4.2%→0% at 1500/3000/6000 nodes); with only 6 positives, UW is underpowered. Two honest caveats bound the anchor itself: (1) these are in-silico monodomain Mitchell–Schaeffer verdicts with a simulator-scaled "sustained ≥600 ms" cutoff, not clinical 30 s/1 min endpoints, so the anchor tests base-rate plausibility, not numerical equivalence; and (2) because the clinical range is so protocol-wide (~5–85%), a broad swath of rates could be defended post hoc. Critically, neither rate touches the project's central claim — a predictive null whose spine (validity radius ρ and the ρ ~ N⁻¹ scaling law) is computed from the graph Laplacian and requires no simulator label at all.
synthesis.spine_defense: The core result is label-independent in a precise sense — but narrower than "the linear biomarker provably cannot work," and the honest version is stronger for admitting the narrowing. The label-free skeleton is genuine and computed from the graph Laplacian L alone, with no simulator: on real atria the spectral gap λ₃−λ₂ is tiny (validity-radius scan 0.0002–0.004; rho_scaling atrial gap 0.021 at n=424 → 0.001 at n=7020) and collapses ~N⁻¹ (fitted exponent −1.05, matching the 2-manifold Weyl exponent −1.0), so the validity radius ρ = ‖ΔL‖/(λ₃−λ₂) ≈ 2422 is ~10³× past the empirical ρ*≈3. By Davis–Kahan (sin∠(φ₂,φ₂′) ≤ √2·ρ) the single Fiedler vector φ₂ rotates into φ₃ and every φ₂-derived quantity is ill-conditioned. What this PROVES, label-free, is exactly one thing: the first-order single-vector SFI is a numerically INVALID estimator of Δλ₂ on real tissue — classical perturbation theory, no ground-truth label required. It does NOT, by itself, prove non-predictiveness, and three joints must be conceded rather than papered over. (i) ρ's numerator ‖ΔL‖ carries the clinical Δw=0.36 knob (Heida 2021 PMID 34198544; the PMID/journal are real, the underlying ~20% CV-slowing figure is as-cited, not independently re-confirmed) and is fibrosis-weighted, so ρ scales linearly with Δw and shares the label's dominant substrate — meanwhile the classifier consumes SFI as a per-region RANKING covariate whose ordering is largely invariant to the global Δw magnitude, so ρ indicts a magnitude estimate of Δλ₂, not the ranking feature actually scored (a biased estimator can still rank). (ii) ρ only kills the single-vector variant; the well-posed subspace SFI (basis-independent, valid at any ρ, SFI_THEORY §5/§9.3) is ALSO null (ΔAUC +0.0028 at 55k FHN; ~4150 cases to detect), and it is killed by feature REDUNDANCY with λ₂-alone/min-cut/percolation — a LABEL-dependent empirical finding, not ρ. (iii) ρ proves "SFI ≠ true Δλ₂," a linear-algebra fact, not "SFI ⊥ inducibility"; the bridge needs the premise that λ₂-fragility is the axis relevant to reentry, which the frozen prereg itself denies ("governed by wavelength, source–sink mismatch and unidirectional block — never by λ₂", PRE_REGISTRATION.md:121–123), and whose only physical warrant (Pecora–Carroll master-stability, PRL 1998) concerns oscillator SYNCHRONIZATION — the opposite dynamical regime from reentrant wavebreak. The defensible statement is therefore TWO claims that must never proxy for each other: (A) label-free — first-order SFI is provably an invalid Δλ₂ estimator on real atria (ρ ≫ ρ*), and this survives ANY distrust of the labeller because it consumes no simulator verdict; and (B) label-dependent — SFI adds no incremental inducibility signal over standard connectivity features, established on IDENTICAL labels in both arms (so the RELATIVE null is invariant to the labeller's absolute calibration or resolution) and corroborated by the exact and subspace SFI also failing. The word to drop is "provably cannot work"; and ρ ≫ 1 is nearly generic for any diffuse perturbation on a large diffusive mesh (ρ ~ O(N)), so it is a scope statement about real tissue, not a discriminating screening test. Bottom line: the core survives a hostile judge who fully distrusts the labeller — the relative null and the ρ/scaling spine both hold — but the survival is because the null is established relatively and the spine is a Δλ₂-estimator-validity result, not because a single label-free theorem forbids the biomarker.
